# SK2142 — The value passed for the parameter is overwritten before it is read

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

Every path through the member assigns the parameter before anything reads it, so the value the caller passed is discarded unused.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |
| Supersedes | S1226 |

## Why

A parameter that is written before it is read is an argument the caller computed, passed, and never had used. Either the body was meant to use it and an assignment was put in the wrong place, or the author wanted a local and reused the parameter's name to avoid inventing one — and those are opposite defects with the same shape. The reason this is worth a warning rather than a hint is that the call site still reads as though the value matters: every caller is doing work whose result is thrown away one line into the callee, and nothing at the call site can show that.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
void Render(string path) {
    path = Path.Combine(Root, "default.txt");
    Write(path);
}
```

Write:

```csharp
void Render(string path) {
    var resolved = Path.Combine(Root, path);
    Write(resolved);
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **The verdict is Roslyn's data flow, not a syntactic scan, which is what makes the conditional cases right by construction.** `if (flag) { x = 1; } Use(x);` reads the incoming value on the other path and is silent; so are `x += 1`, `x++` and `x ??= y`, all of which read before they write. The finding is exactly "the parameter is written inside the body and its incoming value flows in nowhere". ⚠ **`ref`, `out` and `in` parameters are excluded, and excluding them is load-bearing rather than cautious**: an `out` parameter *must* be assigned before it is read — that is its contract — and a data-flow analysis reports every correct `out` parameter as having its incoming value discarded, because it has none. Measured, not assumed: both shapes were run through `AnalyzeDataFlow` and both came back looking exactly like the defect. ⚠ **A captured parameter is declined.** Roslyn's data flow over a body containing a lambda or a local function that touches the parameter is not ordered the way the reader is, so a parameter in the `Captured` set is left alone even when the write looks unconditional — that is where this analysis stops and it is stated rather than hidden. ⚠ **Parameters only.** `S1226` also covers caught exceptions and `foreach` variables; those are separate shapes with their own legitimate uses and are not part of this rule. Bodyless declarations — abstract, extern, partial defining declarations, interface members — and generated code have nothing to analyse. **Report-only**, because the repair is a choice between "the caller's value was meant to be used" and "this wanted a local", and the rule cannot know which; that is the same reason `SK2090`–`SK2092` ship without fixes.
